one_line_contribution: On ALFWorld, rewrite the object-placement rule at three binding scopes (one receptacle per class globally, per (scene,class), per game) and show that the scope fixes the smallest cached static prefix that matches top-k retrieval — a sentence, a table, or nothing but the instance's own planted duplicate — thereby splitting a measured retrieval gain into a compilable part and a near-duplicate-leakage part.
closest_prior_work: Closest verified methodological threat: ExecRetrieval (arXiv:2609.01865, verified via hf) plants controlled, execution-verified near-clone variants of each query's canonical solution into the retrieval pool to measure whether retrieval discriminates correct from near-duplicate-but-wrong items. That is the same 'plant a controlled duplicate and read off the effect' move, but on code retrieval, scored on ranking rather than task success, with no compiled-static arm and no scope manipulation, so it does not make this proposal's claim. For the P6(b) branch specifically, The Compliance Trap (arXiv:2607.10608, verified via s2, E-P-R trajectory-level framework for how agents consume conflicting retrieved memory) already shows early adoption of conflicting memory and weak recovery; P6(b) is a narrower special case (does a correct rank-1 self-duplicate survive two contradicting neighbours), so that branch is an increment rather than a new finding. EvoMemBench (arXiv:2605.18421, verified via s2) uses 'memory scope' for in-episode vs cross-episode and reports long-context beating memory methods — adjacent to the whole-bank arm, a different axis; the proposal is right that it does not manipulate binding scope or duplicate rate. AgentCL (arXiv:2606.02461, verified via s2) supplies controlled task streams and transfer-gain metrics but no compiled-prompt arm. SWE-ContextBench (arXiv:2602.08316, verified via s2, 10 cit) shows retrieved prior experience helps most on hard tasks but draws relatedness from dependency links rather than manipulating it. No verified paper makes the central claim.
strongest_objection: The headline is largely constructed rather than discovered, and the automated entailment check reaches the same conclusion for P6(a). Instance-scope relocation is defined so that game A's receptacle is uninformative about game B's; 'no spillover' (N(0.5) = residual(0)) is therefore what the construction guarantees, and the only escape route — generic search-strategy transfer from seeing other instances' trajectories — is never isolated by an arm. Worse, the added foreign duplicates can only displace same-scene train items at ranks 1-3, pushing N(0.5) down, so the prediction is protected from both sides. The same objection applies to the ladder's spine: at global scope the compiled sentence is by construction an information-complete statement of the relocation rule, and at instance scope the proposal declares that no sub-linear prefix exists rather than testing it ('the O(instances) duplicate-row table ... is not run'). What remains genuinely empirical is only whether Qwen3-32B can execute a stated rule, look up a row, or copy a 25-step expert plan — a prompt-format and lookup-ability result, not a result about memory. Second, the title promises an audit of how much of a memory gain is leakage, but no published benchmark's duplicate rate is measured anywhere in the design; s is hand-set to {0, 0.5, 1} and the slope over s is explicitly demoted to descriptive, so the paper cannot say what fraction of any real reported memory gain is leakage. Third, P5's +28 threshold is anchored to nothing measured: static3-relocated's level under the 25-step relocated regime is unknown, and with the node's observed ~0.87 ceiling a strong static arm could force falsification for headroom reasons rather than for the claim. Fourth, P7 confounds 'the whole bank cannot replace the query' with prefix length and serial position — an ~11k-token 80-item prefix versus a ~430-token one — and blind1's -3 net length bound was measured at 430 tokens, so it does not cover this regime.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Demote P6(a) and promote P0 and P4 to the headline: 'Measurement C's +17.2 net retrieval residual compiles into ~20 class-location sentences (or a 274-row table)' is the result that is neither entailed nor already known, and it needs no relocation machinery. (2) Make the no-spillover claim earn its keep with the bank-composition control the entailment check names: hold bank size and rank-1-3 composition fixed and vary only whether the extra same-scene items are other games' exact duplicates or matched non-duplicate trajectories, with s at 0.25 and 0.75, so the strategy-transfer channel is shown to exist before its absence is claimed. (3) Run the instance-scope row table (one (game -> receptacle) row per eval game, ~274 rows, the same size as the scene-scope table already budgeted) as a confirmatory cell rather than declaring it out of scope; it is one cell and it is the only arm that can refute 'instance scope requires a query'. (4) Anchor P5 to the measured static3-relocated level in the same cell and state the achievable ceiling under the 25-step budget, or restate P5 as a fraction of headroom. (5) Add a position/length control to P7: the same 80-item prefix with the duplicate at rank 1, middle and last, plus an 80-item prefix with the duplicate removed, so 'no query' is separated from lost-in-the-middle (cf. 2605.27105, 2505.15561). (6) Measure the actual (goal, scene, init) duplicate rate of at least one published agent-memory benchmark stream and place it on the s axis, so the leakage index refers to something outside this design.
missing_baseline: The instance-scope compiled row table — one (game -> target receptacle) row per eval game as a single cached static prefix, at most 274 rows, i.e. exactly the size of the scene-scope table the plan already runs. The proposal explicitly declines it ('the O(instances) duplicate-row table is the whole-bank arm in row form and is not run'), but it is the direct test of the ladder's punchline that instance scope admits no static substitute, and it is the arm most likely to break it: if a reader can find its own game's row among 274 rows as easily as its scene's row among 274 rows, then everything compiles and the ladder collapses into 'retrieval is never necessary here'. Omitting an arm that costs one cell and is the sole falsifier of the top-level claim will read to a reviewer as protecting the result. Secondary omission: a content-matched non-duplicate bank-composition control at instance scope (fix bank size and rank composition, swap other games' exact duplicates for matched non-duplicate trajectories), without which P6(a) has no arm that could produce its falsifier.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is unusually good for this pipeline — four query classes with channels named, IDs returned, and EvoMemBench's in-episode/cross-episode 'scope' correctly distinguished from binding scope — so I judge it credible rather than thin. My own searches all went through channel (a), the s2cli.py command (S2 + HF together); every keyword query was answered by the hf side, and the id verifications by the s2 side. (1) mechanism, --recent: 'binding scope duplicate rate experience bank retrieval gain leakage agent memory' -> [hf] 2607.14159 MemoHarness, 2607.13157, 2607.10608 Compliance Trap, 2606.24775, 2606.24595 MEMPROBE, 2605.12493 LongMemEval-V2, 2605.11325 Tenure (typed schemas with 'scope isolation', but a belief-store design paper, not a scope manipulation), 2602.08316 SWE-ContextBench, 2512.16962 MemoryGraft — none manipulates duplicate rate or binding scope, none reports a compiled-static arm. (2) mechanism, all years: 'controlled near-duplicate rate in retrieval corpus how much of few-shot gain is duplicate leakage' -> [hf] 2609.01865 ExecRetrieval (planted execution-verified near-clones; closest method), 2608.22856 repeat-aware answer-churn audit, 2608.03089, 2606.24998, 2606.07597, 2605.27105 (RAG document-position and context-size reproduction — bears directly on P7's confound), plus older dedup/poisoning work; no agent-memory duplicate-rate manipulation. (3) closest named method: 'ExpeL agent experience learning ALFWorld retrieved trajectories versus compiled rules static prompt' -> [hf] 2308.10144 ExpeL, 2605.16986 Skills on the Fly, 2601.22758 AutoRefine, 2505.00234 self-generated in-context examples, 2410.07484 / 2504.15785 WALL-E rule learning, 2010.03768 ALFWorld — several compile rules from trajectories, none reports the compiled artifact as a token-matched substitute for retrieval under a scope manipulation. (4) home vocabulary, --recent: 'does retrieval of demonstrations beat a fixed prompt when test example is a near duplicate of a demonstration' -> [hf] 2608.22856, 2606.22338 RoboMME-Interference, 2606.26511, 2606.05588, 2606.07597 — empty on the specific claim. (5) --recent: 'fraction of agent memory improvement attributable to task overlap dose response duplicate task stream ablation' -> [hf] 2608.07169, 2608.06811, 2607.10608, 2607.08716, 2606.14571, 2602.02196 TIDE, 2601.11653 — empty on the specific claim. IDs I verified: 2511.20857 Evo-Memory (s2, 123 cit), 2512.10696 ReMe (s2, ACL, 55 cit), 2605.18421 EvoMemBench (s2, 7 cit, two axes memory scope/content as the proposal describes), 2606.02461 AgentCL (s2, 1 cit, controlled task streams + MemProbe as described), 2602.08316 SWE-ContextBench (s2, 10 cit), 2607.10608 Compliance Trap (s2, E-P-R framework as described), 2107.06499 (s2, ACL, 971 cit), 2411.03923 ConTAM (hf), 2609.01865 ExecRetrieval (hf). Not verified: 2311.04850 (rephrased-sample contamination) and the brief-level ids the novelty argument does not rest on. One caveat the proposal's check misses: it ran no query in the compiled/distilled-skills literature its own brief names (ICAL 2406.14596, SkillEvolBench 2605.24117, MemAPO 2603.21520, CLEAR 2604.07487) even though P2 and P4 are compiled-vs-retrieved claims, and none in the RAG position / long-context literature that governs P7's interpretation (2505.15561, 2605.27105). Those two gaps are where a scoop is most likely sitting, and an empty search I did not run is reported here as not run, not as novelty.
